key_insight: UNIEGO learns richer egocentric video representations by using multiple proxy teachers as mediators, so a model trained only on first-person video can still absorb knowledge from other viewpoints, modalities, and foundation models. The result is a more expressive and transferable representation without requiring extra inputs at deployment.
problem_solved: Egocentric video is inherently limited by a narrow first-person view, making it hard for a single model or modality to capture the full complexity of human actions. This paper addresses how to unify complementary knowledge from diverse sources while keeping inference deployable from egocentric video alone.
method: Uses a hierarchical multi-teacher distillation framework to transfer knowledge into an egocentric student model.
Introduces proxies as mediators, allowing information from other viewpoints, modalities, and foundation models to be distilled indirectly.
Learns a unified representation that is trained with richer supervision but remains usable from egocentric video only at test time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to improve first-person video understanding without changing the deployment setting or requiring extra sensors. It is especially useful for action recognition, wearable AI, and multimodal representation learning where supervision is rich but inference must stay lightweight.

paper_title: UNIEGO: Proxies as Mediators for Unified Egocentric Video Representation Learning
paper_authors: Wenhao Chi, Arkaprava Sinha, Dominick Reilly, Hieu Le, Srijan Das
